model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over the number of iterations for five different models, comparing their convergence behavior. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” is linear and spans from 0 to 140,000 iterations, with tick marks appearing at regular intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” is linear and ranges from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains five lines: the “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with no markers and a solid style; “StrmLLM (n=64)” is a blue line with circle markers and a solid style; “SepLLM (n=64)” is an orange line with triangle markers and a solid style; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” is a green line with square markers and a solid style; and “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” is a red line with diamond markers and a solid style. The “SepLLM (n=128)” model is shown as a dark blue line with star markers and a solid style. All lines start at a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and decrease rapidly, stabilizing around a loss of 2.5 to 2.6 after approximately 60,000 iterations. The “Vanilla” model begins at a loss of approximately 3.4 and drops to about 2.45 by 140,000 iterations. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” model starts at a loss of approximately 3.3 and settles around 2.65. The “SepLLM (n=64)” model begins at a loss of approximately 3.3 and stabilizes around 2.55. The “SepLLM (n=64, H)” model starts at a loss of approximately 3.3 and ends around 2.5. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” model begins at a loss of approximately 3.3 and ends around 2.5. The “SepLLM (n=128)” model starts at a loss of approximately 3.3 and stabilizes around 2.55.
